//: Composite indexes required by Dhakker.
The assistant proxy (assistant-proxy/worker.js, queryFirestoreSupplications)
issues an ARRAY_CONTAINS_ANY query on the language-appropriate tag field
together with equality filters on isActive and verificationStatus.
Firestore requires a composite index for that combination, and the query
FAILS without it. Retrieval failure degrades safely (the assistant returns
its deterministic 'no approved source' response rather than erroring), so a
missing index looks like 'the assistant never finds anything' rather than a
crash — deploy these before expecting grounded answers.
Field order matters: equality filters first, array-contains last.
Deploy with:  firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes

indexes.//: Arabic-language retrieval by the assistant proxy.

Admin review queue: list records awaiting verification, newest first.
Admin audit: verified records by zone, most recently verified first.

//: Ritual-scoped texts (e.g. the Talbiyah) at a given zone. The app
queries appliesToZoneKeys array-contains together with equality
filters on isActive and verificationStatus.
Both filters belong in the QUERY, not in the client: firestore.rules
allows any signed-in user to read `supplications` with no
per-document predicate. Rules are not filters — whatever the query
leaves unconstrained really does arrive on the device.
Without this index the query FAILS, and the catch in
getSupplicationsByZone turns that failure into an empty list: the
Talbiyah would silently not appear at any miqat, with no error
anywhere. Deploy before expecting it to show up.
